title: Adhesive bonding made easy: how Adhese 2 makes your filling appointments simpler
html:
Etch or no etch? Dry or moist? Light-cure or dual-cure? Adhese 2 is designed to take the decisions out of the adhesive bonding step, so the rest of your filling therapy can run to plan.

Imagine a Tuesday afternoon. You are going to restore a Class II cavity in a lower molar, and you are wondering whether the preparation area is as dry as it should be. In addition, you will have to cement a crown in a while. Even before you have inserted any filling material you have had to make several decisions: etching protocol, how moist dentin is too moist, which adhesive is suitable for the situation, and is the bottle that you just used still within its shelf life.

All these are not difficult decisions but rather the complexity that comes from multiple decisions that make the direct restoration appointment complicated and consume your precious time.

Three questions for your adhesive bonding protocol

  • How many adhesives do you have in your practice, and does everyone on your team agree on which of them to use in different situations?
  • How much adhesive do you dispense without ever applying it on a tooth surface?
  • What do you do when light access is not optimal, and does this require another product or an additional procedure?

If your honest answers are ‘too many’, ‘too much’ and ‘it depends’ respectively, it is time to think of simplification of your bonding procedure.

One adhesive to suit any etching protocol

Adhese 2 by Ivoclar is a versatile adhesive designed to meet any clinical need. This product is universal in the sense that it can be used in total etch, selective enamel etch and self-etch techniques as well as in light-cured and dual-cured composites. According to Ivoclar, it ensures bond strengths above 25 MPa on enamel and dentine no matter which etching protocol you use.*

Adhese 2 is also compatible with moist and dry dentin, which eliminates the guesswork between etching and bonding. When each dentist in the practice prefers a different protocol, a universal adhesive enables the whole team to use only one product.

Two other important features for a better clinical outcome

Adhese 2 has an integrated desensitising feature and allows applying a layer of 10 µm or less in thickness, which reduces the risk of postoperative sensitivity and guarantees an accurate fit of indirect restorations as well as a perfectly smooth appearance of direct fillings.

Click, apply, go on

Adhese 2 comes in Ivoclar’s VivaPen which allows dispensing the product right in the patient’s mouth. There is no mixing well to fill and no pre-dispensing, which reduces waste of the material. There is a fill-level indicator in the pen that shows you how much of the product is left. Ivoclar claims that using the pen allows making up to four times more single-tooth applications per ml compared with bottle systems.

The new advantage of Adhese 2: dual cure mode

The difference from the previous version of Adhese, Adhese Universal, is the possibility to use Adhese 2 in the dual-cure mode. The blue DC cannula contains the coating with a co-initiator, so when you use it in combination with a dual-curing composite you get both chemical and light curing without a separate activator. Ivoclar claims that Adhese 2 is the first adhesive that allows applying in dual-cure mode with the help of VivaPen.

This will be the most important feature when light cannot reach the restoration area, e.g., when luting indirect restorations or endodontic posts with Variolink Esthetic DC. The pen that helped you to perform the filling in the morning will come in handy for cementation in the afternoon.

How Adhese 2 fits into your filling workflow

Bonding is only one of the steps in a workflow, and Adhese 2 belongs to Ivoclar’s coordinated Direct Restorative Workflow consisting of OptraGate 2/OptraGate Dry Control for isolation, Adhese 2 for bonding, Tetric plus for restoration, Bluephase PowerCure for curing and OptraGloss for polishing in one step. All these products are designed to work together, and simplification of one of the steps will not complicate another.
